newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINLAND SHOULD CANCEL BANK SUPPORT DECISION -MPS.
newsitem.headline: FINLAND SHOULD CANCEL BANK SUPPORT DECISION -MPS.

text.p: A parliament decision made in February 1993 guaranteeing unlimited state support to Finnish banks should be cancelled, the legislature's state finance committee said in a statement received on Thursday.

The committee had been asked to submit its views on a government report to parliament dealing with state support to banks. The committee also referred to planned legislation to cap state guarantees on bank deposits.
"Putting a limit on the protection of deposits is meaningless unless the bank support decision made by parliament is removed," the state finance committee said.

It pointed at a parliament decision on February 23, 1993, which said: "Parliament requires the State of Finland to guarantee that Finnish banks are able to meet their commitments on time under all circumstances. Whenever necessary, Parliament shall grant sufficient appropriations and powers to be used by the Government for meeting such commitments."
The state finance committee said the conditions already existed to cancel this decision.
But even the formal cancellation of the state's unlimited bank support guarantee would not remove the problem of "indirect deposit protection" enjoyed by "big banks," the committee said.
In 1991, the Bank of Finland and the finance ministry thought that the now defunct SKOPBank was too big a bank to be allowed to face liquidity problems.

The authorities assumed full control of SKOPBank in the autumn of 1991 in the first step of the banking sector crisis which led to parliament's full support decision, and later to centralisation in the sector through mergers.
Each of Finland's current three big banking groups are bigger than SKOPBank was.
"The government should investigate in which way the deposit protection could be limited so that it would apply in reality to the big banks, too," the state finance committee said.

The government's autumn 1996 bank support report to parliament put the gross amount of pay-outs of state bank support at end-July at 69.95 billion markka, and the net amount considering returned payments at 51.58 billion.
In addition, the government has given guarantees worth 28.05 billion markka, and made decisions in principle for guarantees worth another 3.70 billion markka.
The finance ministry has esimated that the final loss to the state will be in the region of 45-50 billion markka.

The state finance committee said it was obvious that Finnish state support to banks had become clearly more expensive -- over 10 percent relative to GDP -- than in Sweden (five percent) and Norway (two percent).
"Although Finland's economic recession has been clearly deeper than in Sweden or Norway, it is still justified to ask why the difference in bank support is so significant," the committee said.
